masters.syllabus_source: source-01: WLD-114 Genco syllabusPCCC_2026-27 For Curriculum Committee.docx SHA256 BA7318644E77EAB2C1487D5A075D6986B297DE84B375E97B1BEE639D50D78DAA

masters.calendar_resolution: 55 instructional days per supplied extended guide and user request; no dates imported. Official night 23/24-day calendar remains unresolved.

outcomes.text: Safely operate Torchmate 4X00 CNC plasma equipment following Torchmate Academy standards.
Configure FlexCut 80 consumables and settings for various materials and thicknesses.
Use VMD SP2 to perform startup, shutdown, alignment, AVHC adjustments, nesting, and first-cut procedures.
Create and modify CAD files using Torchmate CAD including shapes, paths, offsets, nesting, and GM-file output.
Diagnose and correct cut-quality issues such as bevel, dross, kerf variation, and torch misfires.
Perform daily, monthly, and as-needed maintenance procedures based on Torchmate Academy modules.
Produce a CNC-cut project demonstrating dimensional accuracy and proper toolpath preparation.

masters.adaptation_note: The supplied WLD-114 committee syllabus controls course identity and lists 2 credits. WLD-CNC-P is mapped to WLD 114 because the supplied title, Torchmate content and WLD-115 pairing match; this is a documented content mapping, not a registrar change. The legacy 08:00 start is replaced by the requested PVHS section windows. Maintenance product instructions are held for installed-manual verification. Academy title/access verification and the separately named AWS safety certificate remain prerequisites to claiming completion.

days.title: Safety First (complete in one day) + Lab Standards
days.week: WEEK 1 – Safety (Complete Day 1) + Machine Setup Foundations
days.weekly_coaching: Safety is completed Day 1. After that, every day starts with a quick safety/inspection routine before any motion.
activities: Torchmate Academy: Safety First module + quiz completion
Lab walkthrough: gantry, rails, slats, air system, consumables, emergency stop
Teach the ‘no surprises’ rule: announce motion, hands clear, eyes up
Introduce file hygiene: naming rules + where files live
days.coaching: Make Day 1 count. Students should leave knowing exactly what ‘safe CNC’ looks like.
source_activities: Torchmate Academy: Safety First module + quiz completion
Lab walkthrough: gantry, rails, slats, air system, consumables, emergency stop
Teach the ‘no surprises’ rule: announce motion, hands clear, eyes up
Introduce file hygiene: naming rules + where files live
days.objective: By the end of this meeting, produce and explain safety response and supervised inspection record: baseline and stated acceptance target. Demonstrate the assigned safety and readiness checks and explain when to stop; instructor observation is required before any machine authorization.
days.instructor_prep: Display the drawing/procedure and acceptance criteria for safety first (complete in one day) + lab standards. Stage the listed materials and a relevant example. Review each student’s prior attempt and outstanding hold.
days.safety_focus: Check required PPE, ventilation, fire controls, screens, leads and work area before work. Identify hot material and stop unsafe work immediately. Students report defects; repairs and energy isolation are performed only by authorized personnel under the applicable procedure. No unattended machine, live arc or destructive test. Verify the installed Torchmate 4800/FlexCut 80 configuration, approved consumables, material and cut chart. Instructor releases file, path, alignment, settings and clear work envelope before motion or firing. Follow the installed equipment manual for maintenance and shutdown; the source WD-40 instruction is not adopted without manufacturer confirmation.
days.materials_equipment: Torchmate 4800 and FlexCut 80; installed-controller manual and cut chart; instructor-authorized Academy access; CAD workstation and approved file storage; sample consumables; approved stock; suitable measuring tools; tagged sample cuts; daily inspection sheet.
days.teaching_guidance:
Torchmate Academy: Safety First module + quiz completion
Lab walkthrough: gantry, rails, slats, air system, consumables, emergency stop
Teach the ‘no surprises’ rule: announce motion, hands clear, eyes up
Introduce file hygiene: naming rules + where files live
days.assignment: WLD114-D01: Safety response and supervised inspection record: baseline and stated acceptance target. Submit it with student, section, date, attempt and reference revision.
days.assessment: Instructor-scored items scheduled: torchmate_quizzes. Observe the performance or inspect the evidence before scoring; otherwise leave pending.
days.evidence: Safety response and supervised inspection record: baseline and stated acceptance target
days.instructor_notes: Record observed result, prompt/correction, release scope, unfinished work and next step. Make Day 1 count. Students should leave knowing exactly what ‘safe CNC’ looks like.

segments.title: Focused instruction
segments.instructor_actions: Model the first task using the approved reference: Torchmate Academy: Safety First module + quiz completion Ask students to identify the controlling requirement before proceeding.
segments.student_actions: Identify the standard or drawing requirement and explain the demonstrated step before attempting it.

segments.title: Guided and independent work
segments.instructor_actions: Direct the teaching sequence below, circulate for short checks, and coach one correction at a time. Make Day 1 count. Students should leave knowing exactly what ‘safe CNC’ looks like.
segments.student_actions: Complete the listed tasks within authorized limits. Keep the baseline, make one controlled correction and record what changed.

segments.title: Evidence check
segments.instructor_actions: Inspect safety response and supervised inspection record: baseline and stated acceptance target. Record the evidence ID and hold/release; assign a grade only for an observed scheduled assessment.
segments.student_actions: Submit the assigned evidence and explain the result against the stated criteria.

segments.title: Safe closeout and next step
segments.instructor_actions: Supervise shutdown and cleanup. Verify labels, stored parts/files, actual results and the next correction. Carry unfinished work forward with a hold; never mark competence from elapsed time.
segments.student_actions: Label and store evidence, reset tools and equipment safely, and record the next operation or correction.

days.handoff: Identify approved parts or templates available to WLD 115; do not promise cut parts before the source sequence reaches the required CAD and cutting skills. Use instructor-prepared stock where needed.
days.acceptance: Demonstrate the assigned safety and readiness checks and explain when to stop; instructor observation is required before any machine authorization.
days.remediation: If the student cannot explain the requirement or demonstrate safe readiness, stop the operation. Return to the last verified step, model one correction, then collect a new linked attempt. Preserve earlier evidence.
days.extension: After required evidence is verified, repeat under a controlled changed variable or compare approved examples. Do not advance position, machine authorization or secondary track without instructor release.

masters.title: Introduction to GMAW FCAW and GTAW
masters.syllabus_source: source-02: WLD-115 Genco syllabusPCCC_2026-27 For Curriculum Committee.docx SHA256 4A4927D040F0C0ACCED48D53C965E3CD1CB113543617C68AA27E93AA5A9BA3EB
masters.credit_resolution: Use supplied committee syllabus value 4 for this review edition; registrar metadata is not changed.
masters.calendar_resolution: 55 instructional days per supplied extended guide and user request; no dates imported. Official night 23/24-day calendar remains unresolved.

outcomes.text: Perform safety inspections for GMAW, FCAW, and GTAW equipment.
Correctly set up GMAW, FCAW, and GTAW power sources, guns, torches, and gas systems.
Produce GMAW stringer beads and fillet welds in 1F–4F positions.
Produce FCAW stringer beads and fillet welds following proper parameter control.
Perform GTAW autogenous welds and filler-metal welds on ferrous and non-ferrous metals.
Interpret weld quality indicators and apply corrective adjustments to improve technique.

masters.adaptation_note: The supplied 55-day source uses 190 minutes. This edition retains all 55 day topics and the GMAW/FCAW/GTAW sequence while using 120 minutes per user direction. Reduce repetitions to fit the block; do not skip setup, inspection or safe closeout. The original six-week syllabus still controls outcomes and weights. Ferrous and non-ferrous GTAW evidence is required by the syllabus, even where the guide says introduce as appropriate.

outcomes.text: Plan a complete fabrication workflow from blueprint to final assembly.
Interpret technical drawings and produce accurate cut lists.
Prepare CNC plasma files, nesting, and toolpath verification.
Fabricate assigned components using appropriate welding processes.
Apply tolerances, measurement strategies, and distortion control.
Perform QC inspections and document fabrication processes.
Participate in team assembly and deliver a professional final presentation.

days.title: Orientation, standards, and capstone overview
days.week: WEEK 1 - Launch, blueprint confidence, and capstone setup
days.weekly_coaching: Week 1 sets the culture. Slow the room down, make the workflow visible, and establish that approval gates are part of the build, not an annoyance.
activities: Set course standards for PPE, communication, cleanup, tool control, documentation, and how approvals must happen before material is committed.
Introduce the capstone model: each student or team owns a component that must fit a larger class assembly, so individual mistakes affect the full build.
Walk the class through the production path from print review to final presentation so students see where their work is heading.
Use prior projects, photos, or sample parts to show the difference between a finished fabrication workflow and a pile of random steel.
days.coaching: Tone-setting day. Capstone gets easier when the workflow is predictable from the start.
days.guidance: Do not let this become a vague pep talk. Show the path, name the gates, and make students repeat the sequence back to you.

Maintain material identity, drawing revision, critical dimensions and current release status. Hold unapproved material, first pieces, tack-fit parts and weld-outs at the named checkpoints. Do not grind away required dimensions or conceal an unreviewed defect.

days.week: WEEK 2 - Cut lists, material planning, and layout strategy
days.weekly_coaching: Planning week should feel deliberate, not slow. The point is to build confidence before steel and time get wasted.
activities: Teach cut-list structure: part name, quantity, material, thickness, profile or stock type, and any prep notes tied to the print.
Have students translate their print section into an initial cut list with instructor review before anything is staged.
Review common cut-list failures: missing quantities, vague notes, wrong stock assumptions, and ignored material thickness.
Make students identify what they still need to know before the cut list can be approved.
days.coaching: If they can explain the cut list clearly, they are usually close to being ready to cut.
days.guidance: Treat approval like coaching, not policing. The goal is to catch expensive mistakes while they are still cheap.

activities: Correct dry-fit problems through grind, re-cut, re-clamp, shim, or remake decisions as needed.
Re-check alignment and dimensions after correction rather than assuming the fix worked.
Update packets so the tack phase begins with accurate notes, not optimistic guesses.
Release only those components that are truly ready for controlled tack-up next week.
days.coaching: A calm correction now beats a dramatic repair later.
days.guidance: Do not reward wishful thinking. If the fit is wrong, name it and fix it.

days.title: Tack standards and distortion basics
days.week: WEEK 6 - Tack welding and QC Check #2
days.weekly_coaching: The room should start looking like a real fabrication lab now. Keep tacks deliberate and keep inspection tighter than the students want.
activities: Review tack size, spacing, cleanup, and what a tack must accomplish before weld-out is even considered.
Teach heat input basics, restraint, and why distortion prevention starts at tack-up, not after the part is already warped.
Have students inspect their dry-fit setup one last time before striking an arc.
Tie tack decisions directly to the print and the later weld sequence.
days.coaching: Students often think tacks are disposable. Teach them that bad tacks are expensive.
days.guidance: Watch preparation and restraint, not just the arc. Distortion starts before the puddle does.

days.weekly_coaching: Students usually want to rush here. Keep the work controlled and insist that sequence thinking shows up before arc time.
activities: Review parts that pulled, twisted, or lost fit during weld-out and assign controlled correction methods.
Discuss when to grind, re-tack, shrink, re-clamp, or remake versus when to leave acceptable variation alone.

days.guidance: Do not let cosmetic grinding hide structural sloppiness. Fix the cause first.

days.guidance: Do not let students personalize problems. Treat every mismatch like evidence to be traced.

segments.title: Focused instruction

segments.title: Guided and independent work
segments.instructor_actions: Direct the teaching sequence below, circulate for short checks, and coach one correction at a time. Watch for students trying three changes at once. One change, then verify.

days.title: Final trial assembly and finish alignment
days.week: WEEK 10 - Assembly trials and correction cycle
days.weekly_coaching: This is the tolerance lesson they will actually remember. Keep the room calm, specific, and solution-focused.
activities: Run a second or refined trial assembly with corrected parts and verify that the overall geometry now holds.
Check final alignment, finish compatibility, and whether presentation-facing surfaces remain acceptable.
Identify any last cleanups or low-risk adjustments needed before locking the final plan.
Confirm that the class now understands the final closeout sequence.
days.coaching: A cleaner second trial fit is one of the most satisfying moments in the course.
days.guidance: Use that momentum, but do not get sloppy because the room finally feels hopeful.

segments.student_actions: Explain today’s target, identify hazards and show required readiness checks.

segments.title: Focused instruction
segments.instructor_actions: Model the first task using the approved reference: Coach students through a short professional presentation: what they built, what controlled fit, what went wrong, what was fixed, and what they learned. Ask students to identify the controlling requirement before proceeding.
segments.student_actions: Identify the standard or drawing requirement and explain the demonstrated step before attempting it.

segments.title: Guided and independent work
segments.instructor_actions: Direct the teaching sequence below, circulate for short checks, and coach one correction at a time. Keep them specific. General statements sound weak next to real evidence.
segments.student_actions: Complete the listed tasks within authorized limits. Keep the baseline, make one controlled correction and record what changed.

segments.title: Evidence check
segments.instructor_actions: Inspect presentation outline and evidence-based reflection. Record the evidence ID and hold/release; assign a grade only for an observed scheduled assessment.
segments.student_actions: Submit the assigned evidence and explain the result against the stated criteria.

segments.title: Safe closeout and next step
segments.instructor_actions: Supervise shutdown and cleanup. Verify labels, stored parts/files, actual results and the next correction. Carry unfinished work forward with a hold; never mark competence from elapsed time.
segments.student_actions: Label and store evidence, reset tools and equipment safely, and record the next operation or correction.

days.handoff: Send the paired WLD 150 instructor the component ID, drawing revision, allowed next operation and unresolved holds. WLD 150 retains its own process and test priorities.
days.acceptance: Required and actual dimensions, part identity and drawing revision are recorded as applicable to this phase; the named next operation remains on hold until the instructor records release.
days.remediation: If the student cannot explain the requirement or demonstrate safe readiness, stop the operation. Return to the last verified step, model one correction, then collect a new linked attempt. Preserve earlier evidence.
days.extension: After required evidence is verified, repeat under a controlled changed variable or compare approved examples. Do not advance position, machine authorization or secondary track without instructor release.

days.title: Final presentation, portfolio closeout, and shop reset
days.week: WEEK 11 - Final assembly, documentation, presentation, and closeout
days.weekly_coaching: Finish like a professional shop. The project matters, but so does how the class leaves the room and explains the work.
activities: Run final student presentations and project review using the finished assembly and documentation packets as evidence.
Close the course with reflection on tolerance control, teamwork, rework discipline, and what professional follow-through looked like.
Complete full shop reset: tools returned, scrap handled, project materials stored, and paperwork organized for program records.
End with a visible closeout so the next cohort inherits an orderly room instead of someone else’s mess.

masters.calendar_resolution: 55 instructional days per supplied extended guide and user request; no dates imported. Official night 23/24-day calendar remains unresolved.

outcomes.text: Demonstrate advanced proficiency in a selected welding process across multiple positions.
Prepare certification-level groove test plates in the primary track.
Complete destructive bend testing and interpret results.
Execute accurate joint preparation and fit-up for multi-pass weldments.
Apply pipe welding fundamentals safely and consistently.
Compile a weld portfolio documenting progress and final performance in the primary track.

masters.adaptation_note: Course designation, title, outcomes and 4-credit field identify this as WLD 150 Advanced Processes. The source description says WLD-120 and the co-requisite line repeats WLD-150; this edition uses WLD 150 and the WLD 120 pairing supported by both syllabi scheduling notes, and flags the source errors for institutional correction. The guide leaves minutes local; this edition uses 120 minutes. No online AWS coursework is assigned. Source reference to an original 24-day model does not verify the official night calendar.

days.title: Process review and industry-use comparison
days.week: WEEK 1 - Safety Reset, Process Survey, and Track Advising
activities: Review SMAW, GMAW, FCAW, and GTAW strengths, limitations, typical materials, and where each process shows up in actual work.
Compare process variables students already know versus variables they still confuse or oversimplify.

days.title: Bevel preparation, land, root opening, and edge quality
days.week: WEEK 2 - Primary Track Lock-In, Logs, and Joint Preparation
activities: Demonstrate plate-edge preparation, bevel consistency, land control, and why root opening is not a decorative suggestion.
Have students grind and prepare joints appropriate to their track while you inspect edges before fit-up.
Discuss how poor prep creates fake welding problems that students then misdiagnose as setting issues.
days.coaching: Prep mistakes waste more lab time than most welding mistakes because they poison every pass that follows.
days.guidance: Stop sloppy grinding early. It is cheaper to reset now than explain later why a bad root started three steps back.

days.title: Fit-up, tacking sequence, and distortion basics
days.week: WEEK 2 - Primary Track Lock-In, Logs, and Joint Preparation
activities: Demonstrate fit-up checks, tack placement, restraint strategy, and how tack decisions affect root access and distortion.
Students fit and tack practice joints in their primary track with inspection before any full weld is attempted.
Introduce the habit of checking alignment again after tacking instead of assuming the joint stayed where it was told.
days.coaching: Students love to admire their tacks before checking whether the part actually stayed aligned. Charming. Also useless.
days.guidance: Make them re-measure after tacks. That small annoyance saves whole afternoons.

days.title: 1G groove setup and root-area access
days.week: WEEK 3 - Primary Track 1G Groove Development
activities: Set up 1G groove plates appropriate to each primary track and review body position, travel path, and root-area visibility.
Run short controlled passes with emphasis on setup repeatability instead of trying to finish full plates too early.
Log how each process responds to heat, access, and edge preparation in flat work.
days.coaching: Flat does not mean easy. It just removes excuses so the real habits show up faster.
days.guidance: Watch stance and line-of-travel first. Many “process problems” are still body-position problems.

days.week: WEEK 3 - Primary Track 1G Groove Development
activities: Focus on root control, fusion, penetration behavior, and consistent travel in the primary process.
Require interpass cleaning or surface reset habits appropriate to the process before students continue.
Compare acceptable root behavior to common misses such as incomplete fusion, trapped slag, excess reinforcement, or contamination.
days.coaching: This is the day to slow them down. A rushed root is an argument with physics that physics wins every time.
days.guidance: Keep weld lengths short enough that students can explain what happened in each segment.

days.title: 1G fill and cap discipline
days.week: WEEK 3 - Primary Track 1G Groove Development
activities: Continue 1G groove work with fill-pass planning, cap contour control, and toe tie-in expectations.
Have students record whether each pass improved because of settings, travel, cleaning, fit-up, or simply less panic.
Discuss overbuild, undercut, cold lap, and other signs that the cap is solving the wrong problem badly.
days.coaching: A big cap often means a student is trying to bury weak earlier work under more metal. That trick has a very short career.
days.guidance: Make students plan pass sequence before welding. The hand usually follows the brain when the brain bothered to show up.

days.title: 2G setup, body position, and short segments
days.week: WEEK 4 - 2G Transition and Positional Control
activities: Demonstrate 2G plate setup, sight line, body position, and how gravity starts changing puddle behavior in the primary process.
Have students run short 2G segments rather than full-length passes so technique can be corrected before it drifts too far.
Log the first obvious differences between 1G and 2G control, especially toe fusion and travel stability.
days.coaching: A position change is not just a harder weld. It is a new problem that punishes old laziness faster.
days.guidance: Watch comfort and stance before settings. Twisted bodies make ugly welds in every process.

Have students note where a pass improved because of better cleaning or fit-up instead of assuming the machine suddenly became generous.

days.title: 3G multi-pass development
days.week: WEEK 5 - 3G Vertical Progression and Secondary-Track Eligibility
activities: Build 3G work into planned multi-pass practice with emphasis on shelf control, toe pause, and consistent progression.
Review interpass cleaning and what poor cleanup or poor pause timing looks like in a vertical coupon.
Have students note whether the weld broke down because of heat, hesitation, angle, or sloppy prep.
days.coaching: Students love blaming the machine when the real problem is panic, drift, or impatience. The coupons rarely lie.
days.guidance: Ask where the puddle went and why before they weld again.

days.title: 3G correction and profile control
days.week: WEEK 5 - 3G Vertical Progression and Secondary-Track Eligibility
activities: Use prior 3G coupons to identify profile issues, undercut, lack of fusion, excess buildup, or other recurring defects.
Run a targeted correction pass or coupon with one change in technique or settings and record the result.
Compare acceptable vertical profile to the most common class errors so students build visual judgment, not just muscle memory.
days.coaching: Vertical corrections stick better when students can see the difference side by side instead of hearing another lecture.
days.guidance: Make them keep the bad sample too. Evidence of failure is part of the lesson.

Address process-specific risks such as trapped slag, excessive buildup, contamination, or loss of fusion before they compound.
Have students compare the logic of each pass sequence to what they planned the day before.

days.guidance: Keep the work moving, but do not let pace override cleaning or inspection.

activities: Demonstrate 1G pipe root technique appropriate to each track, with focus on access, travel speed, root opening behavior, and tack management.

Log the first signs of good root control or typical failure patterns such as blow-through, cold root, or inconsistent tie-in.

days.title: Final fit checks, correction passes, and rework
days.week: WEEK 11 - Capstone Weld-Out, Portfolio, and Final Debriefs
activities: Dry-fit or fully check the completed capstone for alignment, function, and fit against the planned tolerances.
Assign correction work where needed and keep it targeted to the easiest valid fix, not the most dramatic one.
Have students record what failed, what was corrected, and what they would change in the sequence next time.
days.coaching: This is the week where “good enough” needs adult supervision.
days.guidance: Keep the corrections honest. The easiest real fix usually beats the heroic bad idea.
